findings.claim: Every test added for `create_run`'s new `batch_id` parameter (`test_a_run_created_outside_a_batch_has_a_null_batch_id`, `test_a_ledger_built_by_the_previous_schema_still_opens_and_writes`) calls it with no `batch_id` argument and asserts the column is NULL. No test ever passes a real, non-null `batch_id` and checks it lands in the row. Replacing the bound tuple `(repo_id, base_sha, batch_id)` with `(repo_id, base_sha, None)` — i.e. silently discarding whatever `batch_id` is passed — keeps every test in this diff green while making the parameter a no-op for the one case (a run created inside a batch) that is the actual reason it exists. `census`/`criteria` don't see this because the acceptance criterion as worded only requires the NULL-default behavior; the reverse case is untested.
